flags: The company sold assets of its Maple Street Biscuit Company (MSBC) business to a third party and closed the remaining MSBC locations. It recorded a loss on sale of business assets of $27,039 (thousands, per MD&A).
In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 the company completed a sale and leaseback of 26 owned Cracker Barrel properties and recorded a net gain of $47,421 (thousands, per MD&A).
The company recorded impairment charges of $21,968 in fiscal 2026 (thousands), compared with $19,772 in fiscal 2025. The 2026 charges covered nine Cracker Barrel locations and sixteen MSBC locations.
no_value_reason: no usable tax rate in the filings

business_model.basis: stated in the MD&A revenue table
business_model.claim: The company runs Cracker Barrel stores, each a full-service restaurant with a gift shop. Restaurant sales were 81.4% of revenue ($2,701,820, table in thousands) and retail sales 18.6% (616,894, table in thousands).
quotes: Each Cracker Barrel store consists of a restaurant with a gift shop.

business_model.claim: Customers are travelers and local diners. 84% of the stores are along interstate highways, and the company operated 655 stores in 43 states, none franchised.
quotes: Our Cracker Barrel stores are intended to appeal to both the traveler and the local customer, and we believe they have consistently been a consumer favorite.
As of September 11, 2026, approximately 84% of our stores are located along interstate highways.

business_model.claim: The Maple Street Biscuit Company (MSBC) concept has been exited. The company sold 35 locations and closed the remaining 16, so it now operates only Cracker Barrel stores.
quotes: As of July 31, 2026, we no longer operated any MSBC locations.

business_model.claim: Restaurant sales move with guest traffic and average check. Comparable restaurant traffic fell 7.6% while average check rose 3.7% (menu pricing up 4.3%), leaving comparable restaurant sales down 4.2% and total revenue down 4.7%.
quotes: Our comparable store restaurant sales decrease in 2026 as compared to 2025 resulted primarily from the guest traffic decrease partially offset by the average check increase.

business_model.claim: Retail sales are made mainly to restaurant guests, so retail follows restaurant traffic. Apparel and Accessories (32%) and Food (19%) were the largest retail categories, and about one-third of retail items were bought directly from vendors in China.
quotes: Our retail sales are made primarily to our restaurant guests.

business_model.claim: Retail cost of goods sold fell to 50.2% of retail revenue, mainly because of tariff refunds of $15,033, partly offset by higher markdowns, discounts and lower initial margin.
quotes: The decrease in retail cost of goods sold as a percentage of retail revenue in 2026 as compared to 2025 resulted primarily from tariff refunds of $15,033 partially offset by higher markdowns, higher discounts and lower initial margin.

business_model.basis: stated in MD&A; the fixed-cost explanation is the company's own wording on deleverage
business_model.claim: The largest cost lines are labor (37.3% of revenue, up from 36.0%), other store operating expenses (25.5%, up from 24.6%) and cost of goods sold (30.9%). Labor and occupancy costs are largely fixed, so lower revenue deleveraged them.
quotes: The increases in store hourly labor and store management compensation as a percentage of total revenue in 2026 as compared to 2025 resulted primarily from lower productivity and the deleverage associated with the decrease in total revenue in 2026 as compared to 2025.

business_model.claim: Food cost is driven by commodity prices. Restaurant cost of goods sold was 26.5% of restaurant revenue, commodity inflation was 2.3%, and management expects about 3.0% next year, with wage inflation of 2.5% to 3.0%.
quotes: We presently expect the rate of commodity inflation to be approximately 3.0% in 2027.

business_model.claim: About 20% of restaurant sales come through off-premise channels (To Go, third-party delivery, catering). Third-party delivery fees are listed among store operating costs.
quotes: Approximately 20% of our restaurant sales are generated through our off-premise channels, which include Individual To Go, Third-Party Delivery and Catering and Occasion.

business_model.claim: The company owns the land and buildings for 330 of its 655 stores and leases the rest. Store occupancy costs rose as a share of revenue, and a sale-leaseback of 26 owned properties produced a net gain of $47,421.
quotes: Of the 655 stores open as of September 11, 2026, we own the land and buildings for 330, while the other 325 properties are either ground leases or ground and building leases.

business_model.basis: stated in the income statement and MD&A
business_model.claim: Reported profit was shaped by one-off items. The operating loss was $(12,470) (thousands) despite a $47,421 sale-leaseback gain, because of a $27,039 loss on the MSBC asset sale and impairment. Net income of $31,675 also included $47,422 of litigation settlement income.
quotes: In the third quarter of 2026, the Company received and recorded $47,422, net of legal fees, pursuant to a settlement agreement resolving interchange fee litigation.

business_model.basis: stated in the cash flow statement; the use of proceeds is stated in the earnings release
business_model.claim: Operations generated cash of 206,204 (thousands), more than capital spending of 117,782 (thousands), and total debt was reduced.
Seasonality drives results. Summer interstate travel lifts profits in the fourth quarter, and retail sales are strongest in the second quarter, which includes the holiday shopping season.
quotes: Retail sales, which are made substantially to our restaurant guests, are historically strongest in the second quarter, which includes the holiday shopping season.

business_model.basis: stated in the earnings release; this is guidance, not a result
business_model.claim: Management's outlook ties revenue to comparable restaurant sales growth with no new store openings.
quotes: Total revenue of $3.325 billion to $3.4 billion including comparable store restaurant sales growth of 3% to 5% and no new store openings

competitive_position.claim: The company has a sizeable, company-operated store base: 655 Cracker Barrel stores in 43 states, none of them franchised. The count is slightly below the prior year, because four stores closed and two opened.
quotes: As of September 11, 2026, we operated 655 Cracker Barrel stores in 43 states.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1; the seasonality point is from P3.
competitive_position.claim: The concept pairs a full-service restaurant with a gift shop and is aimed at both travelers and local customers. About 84% of stores sit on interstate highways, which ties much of the traffic to travel and tourist flows.
quotes: Our Cracker Barrel stores are intended to appeal to both the traveler and the local customer, and we believe they have consistently been a consumer favorite.
As of September 11, 2026, approximately 84% of our stores are located along interstate highways.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3 as management opinion.
competitive_position.claim: Management describes the brand as one of the strongest and most differentiated in the restaurant industry and as a core competitive component of its strategy. This is management's own view, not independent evidence.
quotes: Management believes that the Cracker Barrel brand remains one of the strongest and most differentiated brands in the restaurant industry, and we plan to continue to leverage and build on that strength as a core competitive component of our business strategy.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3 (revenue mix and comparable retail sales); dependence on traffic stated in P3.
competitive_position.claim: The gift shop adds a second revenue stream, 18.6% of revenue, and it is sold mainly to restaurant guests. Retail therefore depends on restaurant traffic, and comparable retail sales fell (5.2)%.
quotes: Our retail sales are made primarily to our restaurant guests.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3 (annual figures) and P4 (quarter).
competitive_position.claim: Demand weakened in fiscal 2026. Comparable restaurant guest traffic fell (7.6)% against (3.0)% the year before, and comparable restaurant sales fell (4.2)%. A 3.7% rise in average check only partly offset the traffic loss.
quotes: Our comparable store restaurant sales decrease in 2026 as compared to 2025 resulted primarily from the guest traffic decrease partially offset by the average check increase.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1, P3 and P2.
competitive_position.claim: Brand-initiative missteps are a named cause of the traffic decline. The new logo and modern test remodels drew negative publicity, and the company reverted to its former logo and discontinued the remodels in the first quarter.
quotes: During 2026, we faced challenges related to negative publicity from brand initiatives related to our previously-announced strategic plan, including the launch of a new logo and modern test store remodels, to which we responded by returning to our former logo and discontinuing the modern test store remodels during the first quarter of 2026.

competitive_position.claim: Weaker sales hurt store-level margins. Labor and related expenses rose to 37.3% of revenue from 36.0%, and other store operating expenses rose to 25.5% from 24.6%. Management ties this to lower productivity and fixed-cost deleverage.
quotes: The increases in store hourly labor and store management compensation as a percentage of total revenue in 2026 as compared to 2025 resulted primarily from lower productivity and the deleverage associated with the decrease in total revenue in 2026 as compared to 2025.

competitive_position.basis: stated in F2, with the cause stated in P3; figures from statements in thousands.
competitive_position.claim: Reported results fell, and one-time items distort the comparison. Total revenue was 3,318,714 against 3,483,684 (table in thousands), a 4.7% decline. Operating income swung to a loss of (12,470) from 55,029. Net income was 31,675 against 46,379, helped by litigation settlement income of (47,422).
quotes: Our operating results declined in 2026 as compared to 2025 primarily due to the decrease in total revenue, the loss on sale of business assets associated with the divestiture of the MSBC business and the impairment and store closing costs discussed above partially offset by the gain recognized on the 2026 sale and leaseback transaction.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (risk) and P3 (expected inflation rates).
competitive_position.claim: Pricing power is limited and cost inflation is a threat. The company positions itself as moderately priced, may be unable to pass on price increases without losing demand, and expects commodity inflation of about 3.0% and wage inflation of 2.5% to 3.0% in the next fiscal year.
quotes: We seek to provide a moderately priced product, and, as a result, we may not seek to or be able to pass along price increases to our customers sufficient to completely offset cost increases without adversely affecting our customers’ demand.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 and P1; the evidence names no specific competitor figures.
competitive_position.claim: Competition is intense and includes off-premise and grocery-style alternatives. About 20% of restaurant sales come through off-premise channels, which includes third-party delivery.
quotes: The restaurant and retail industries are intensely competitive, and we face many well-established competitors.
Approximately 20% of our restaurant sales are generated through our off-premise channels, which include Individual To Go, Third-Party Delivery and Catering and Occasion.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1 (sourcing) and P3 (refund effect); risk language in P2.
competitive_position.claim: Tariffs and China sourcing are a supply-chain exposure, yet tariff refunds helped retail margin in fiscal 2026. About one-third of retail items were bought directly from China, and retail cost of goods sold fell to 50.2% of retail revenue from 51.0%. Tariff refunds of $15,033 (MD&A amounts in thousands) drove the improvement.
quotes: Approximately one-third of our 2026 retail items were purchased directly from vendors in the People’s Republic of China.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3; the loss line also appears in F2.
competitive_position.claim: The company narrowed its focus to the core brand by exiting Maple Street Biscuit Company (MSBC). It sold 35 locations, closed the remaining 16, and recorded a loss on the sale of $27,039 (MD&A amounts in thousands).
quotes: Simultaneously with the asset sale, the Company closed its remaining sixteen MSBC restaurant locations on July 20, 2026 as part of its focus on its core Cracker Barrel brand and improve profitability.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P5 (transition) and P3 (proxy costs).

quotes: In 2026, we incurred $4,072 in costs related to a proxy contest in connection with the Company’s 2025 annual shareholders meeting held on November 20, 2025.
